message:
Open on a Home screen; Home button on every screen

- A saved game now opens on the Home screen (Continue with the airline,
  date and cash; New game; Best runs; Save code; Open the wall) instead of
  dropping straight into the run.
- Saves from before the calendar update say they carry on from the nearest
  point in the story.
- The top bar's Menu is now "⌂ Home", and full-screen task and results
  screens get a small "⌂ Home" button in the bottom-left corner.
- Old saves' history is given dates and the daily ledger is rebuilt from
  it, fixing a chart error after migration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Step 2: time speeds up from days to weeks to months; capital takes time

The script becomes 32 beats on calendar dates (Launch day 12 May 2030 to
Airline of the Year, May 2032).

Time and decisions:
- Days 1-5 are hands-on as before.
- "Your airline is settling down" lets the weekend run by itself, then weeks
  are managed one at a time.
- From July 2030 the pupil manages months: Simulate next month, Run 3
  months, or Run until the target plane is affordable.
- Runs stop at the next beat that needs the CEO (alert first, then HQ).
- A decision in weeks or months lands on the first day of the coming run.
- The second plane comes at the Year 1 Review (or sooner once the target is
  affordable with the emergency money kept), and no more often than every
  three months.

Forecasting:
- Before a run: about £X a day x days, about £X a month x months, or the
  saving-for-a-plane table (cash - emergency money, price - that, still
  needed / profit a month, rounded up).
- Afterwards, forecast against actual with the reasons they differ.
- Run screen on HQ and wall (MON ✓ ... / JUL ✓ ...); weekly and monthly
  results slides; half-year and Year 1 reviews to set the emergency money
  and the plane to save for.

Economy:
- Each plane has daily running costs; trip costs are closer to real.
- In weeks and months an empty tank is topped up at market price plus 10p.
- Planes are repriced so the next one is months of profit: one Twin Otter
  makes about £9-22k a month, the Saab (£45k) is affordable around
  February 2031 and the ATR (£75k) at the Year 1 Review. Long-haul planes
  run into the £k/£m range, each paying back in about a year on its best
  route.
- Route cards show how many people your other planes already carry.
- A plane that loses money two periods running can be moved.

HQ and wall follow the period (labels, buttons, saving-for bar, finance
chart by day, week or month, milestones, simulating mode).

A daily ledger and per-period history replace per-round history. Older
saves restart at the matching beat.

New HQ dashboard and Operations Wall built into the game; dates replace rounds

Step 1 of the HQ / Operations Wall brief, wired into the game with real data.

- Calendar: the pupil never sees "Round". Launch day is Sunday 12 May 2030,
  Day 1 is Monday 13 May 2030; the top bar, task headers, results, news and
  teacher panel all use dates and days.
- Mid-blue style with square panels: navy structure, cyan highlights, amber
  for money and the main action, red only for alerts. Notched corners removed.
- HQ dashboard: KPI cards (cash, yesterday's profit, reputation, fuel
  position), today's briefing with "Operate today's flights", network map with
  Routes / Demand / Profit / Opportunities layers, fleet, route performance,
  14-day finance chart with tooltip, fuel, and intelligence (situations, not
  solutions). Fits 1920x1080 and 1366x768 with no scrolling (tabs on laptops).
- Executive alert screen for events: simulation paused, CEO decision.
- Operations Wall replaces the four-quarter IWB screen: a fixed 1920x1080
  stage scaled to fit, departures and arrivals boards, the map at about half
  the screen, a status strip and news ticker. Modes switch by themselves:
  live, executive alert (zoom, flash, dim), daily results, welcome to the
  fleet, milestones. It shows the situation, never the numbers to calculate.
- One state, two views: W or the Operations Wall button shows the wall on the
  same screen; Return to HQ, W or Esc goes back. Split view removed.
- Each day's history now keeps passengers, seats, trips and a per-route
  breakdown; events keep the day's history in step.

HQ dashboard UI explorations (standalone prototypes)

Four self-contained HQ mock-ups with game-scale sample data and a
comparison index, for choosing the HQ's visual direction before wiring:
- 01 mid-blue (recommended), 02 light and airy, 03 dark premium,
  04 operations command; same content in each: header, navigation,
  KPI cards with sparklines and count-ups, Europe route map (game's
  outlines; route/demand/profit tabs, moving planes), fleet, route
  performance, finance chart with tooltip, fuel and operations, alerts,
  and a Start the day button with today's decision.
- hq-ui-options-index.html: thumbnails, one-line ideas, recommendation.
- src/: shared CSS, widgets, mock data and theme/layout sources.
No changes to the game itself.

Split view and test mode for teacher testing; ATR 72 in the fleet choice

- ?split (or Main menu / teacher panel): game and whiteboard side by
  side, each kept at its real 16:9 shape and scaled down, laptop pane
  switchable between 1920x1080 and 1366x768, swap sides, full screen.
  The shell relays messages between the two panes.
- Test mode (teacher panel or ?test): a TEST bar with Answer this one,
  Fill table, Skip screen and Auto-answer. Auto-answer fills each sum
  about 0.7 s after it opens; decisions stay with the player and
  filled answers don't count towards the typed total.
- Round 3's plane choice compares Twin Otter, Saab 340 and ATR 72
  (7 typed answers that round); later fleet offers show three planes.

Agent style back, landing report as slides, second plane in round 3

- Style: back to the notched glowing panels, uppercase header bars with a
  status dot and amber numbers. The embedded Atkinson font is gone: words
  use the system sans and numbers Courier New, so zeros have no slash.
  Questions, stories and tables stay in mixed case at CR4 sizes.
- Landing report is now a short presentation: one point per slide, with
  count-up figures, seat bars filling, forecast-vs-actual bars, one
  reason per slide, stars and reviews; Next, Back, Skip, arrow keys.
- Balance: routes gain passengers each round (growth/cap in data-world;
  Dublin starts at 40). Round 3 offers a second plane in the round
  (compare two planes, then pick its route; it flies that day). If he
  carries on, the option returns every other round while he has one
  plane. Red Kite moves to round 4.
- "How many trips?" is only offered when one plane can't carry everyone;
  if forced, it says everyone fits instead of dividing by more seats.
- After any fuel purchase the tank is checked again, so trips are never
  grounded for want of fuel.

CR4 Stages 1-3: clarity and decision-led rounds

Reading and layout: Atkinson Hyperlegible embedded, 22px text and 32px
numbers, mixed case, no letter-spacing or scanlines behind text, task
panels at least 90% wide, no scrolling at 1920x1080 or 1366x768, and a
three-size text setting saved with the run. Focus mode hides the top bar,
strip and menu buttons on every task screen.

Tables: plain labels, every operand is a row, amber outline on the open
cell and cyan on the numbers it uses, the sum said as a coloured sentence
beside the pad, the next cell opens itself, choices move to the side
panel when the sums are done, "What's in this?" on trip costs. No bars,
no "fits N trips", no Madrid before it unlocks (also on the IWB map).

Rounds: HQ with today's news and one Start the day; "What will you do?"
with Carry on always offered; the table only if he acts; trips in two
steps with a Fly / Don't fly decision; fuel as a decision first; a quick
income sum when the price table doesn't open; a short tank always leads
to buying fuel. Captain's challenge reworded. Setup prices £80/£100/£120.

Stage A: one shared time module (out + turnaround away + back, home
turnaround between trips) used by every screen; the eight CR2 time cases

economics where they were.
Stage B: planning desk (demand as people icons with plane-load brackets,
How many trips table, Set the price table, day timeline, compare two

Clear Skies 30-round world from the workbook; checkpoint; long-haul days

Rounds, events, challenges and rival fares generated from the Clear
Skies 30 Rounds workbook (five acts, 13 events, 15 challenges). Rival
undercuts target the route the pupil flies. Round 12 is a mid-season
checkpoint that snapshots the run to Best runs; round 30 is the finale.
A trip longer than the day is allowed as a plane's only trip and lands
next day; clock answers are checked on the 24-hour clock. Fuel chart
labels every fifth round over long seasons.

Daily schedules, route-aware rival, live market IWB, Present rework

Each plane now flies a planned day of trips (out and back, turnaround
between), with a Plan the day task and a timeline calculation. A route's
passengers are shared across the day's trips. Fares persist and the fare
task is only needed when the route is new or the rival moves; fuel is
only needed when the tank is short; the gated calculation never repeats
the same sum twice. Rival events target the route the pupil actually
flies. IWB: finances move to HQ; the fourth quadrant is a live market
chart (fuel by round vs what was paid, fares vs rival); board shows one
row per trip and planes fly out and back on the map. HQ redesigned with
briefing strip, roomier desk and day timelines. Present opens the IWB
window first, then full screen on the next tap.

Change Request 1: HQ desk, fuel tank, consequences, honest outcomes, fleet ladder, menu, setup additions, question bank

Rounds now run from an HQ screen with task cards the pupil opens in any
order; flights happen every round regardless, with exactly one gated
calculation attached to one task. Fuel is a persistent tank drained by
every flight and valued at the price paid; flights the tank cannot cover
stay on the ground. Briefings reference past decisions. Landing screens
use honest per-flight outcomes (FULL FLIGHT, DELAYED, DIVERTED,
CANCELLED, NO FUEL); 'Cleared for take-off' is only the gate message.
Visual pass: two fonts, one shared style block, flat IWB quadrants with
real gutters. Fleet ladder adds Saab 340, ATR 72, E190 and A220 (12
planes). Main menu with Continue / New game (confirmed, run recorded) /
Best runs. Setup adds a tail-fin motif, a home-airport choice with
landing fees, and the starting fuel purchase. Teacher panel gains a
generated, printable question bank. New Present button fullscreens the
laptop and opens the IWB window fullscreen on the second display via the
Window Management API, with a one-tap fallback.
